# fastkcv

R package · companion to gstat

Fast, exact cross-validation for global kriging

[`kcv()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv.md) takes
the same inputs as
[`gstat::krige.cv()`](https://r-spatial.github.io/gstat/reference/krige.cv.html)
and returns the same output. It factorizes the covariance matrix of the
observations once, instead of refitting the kriging system for every
fold, and the results agree with
[`krige.cv()`](https://r-spatial.github.io/gstat/reference/krige.cv.html)
to numerical precision.

[ Get started](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/articles/fastkcv.md)
[ Reference](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/index.md) [
GitHub](https://github.com/n-c-taylor/fastkcv)

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/n-c-taylor/fastkcv/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/n-c-taylor/fastkcv/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
MIT license R / C++

![fastkcv logo](reference/figures/logo.png)

1,500xfaster leave-one-out than
[`krige.cv()`](https://r-spatial.github.io/gstat/reference/krige.cv.html)
at n = 2,000

1factorization for every fold, no refit per fold

11gstat variogram models, nested and anisotropic

20,000observations in about two minutes

A drop-in for krige.cv()Same formula, locations, data, model, nfold and
beta; the same output columns for data.frame, sf and sp data.

Factorize
once[`kcv_prepare()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_prepare.md)
and
[`kcv_run()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_prepare.md)
reuse one factorization for any number of fold designs.

Spatial fold designsRandom, block and k-means folds, and
[`kcv_metrics()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_metrics.md)
to compare them: RMSE, bias, z-scores, coverage.

Buffered leave-one-outHold out every observation within a radius of each
point, for all points or a subset of targets.

Several responses`cbind(z1, z2) ~ 1` or `kcv_run(prepared, y = )`: many
responses at the same locations from one factorization.

Any covariance
matrix[`kcv_engine()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_engine.md)
runs the same exact computation from a precomputed covariance matrix.

## Installation

Using `pak`:

`pak::pkg_install("n-c-taylor/fastkcv")`

Copy

Using `remotes`:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("n-c-taylor/fastkcv", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

The package contains C++ code, so installing from GitHub needs a
compiler toolchain: Rtools on Windows, the Xcode command line tools on
macOS.

## Example

``` r

library(fastkcv)
library(gstat)
data(meuse, package = "sp")
v <- vgm(0.59, "Sph", 897, 0.05)

# Leave-one-out, as krige.cv(log(zinc) ~ 1, ~ x + y, meuse, model = v)
cv <- kcv(log(zinc) ~ 1, ~ x + y, meuse, model = v)
kcv_metrics(cv)

# One factorization, several fold designs
p <- kcv_prepare(log(zinc) ~ sqrt(dist), ~ x + y, meuse, model = v)
set.seed(1)
kcv_metrics(kcv_run(p, folds = fold_random(~ x + y, meuse, k = 10)))
kcv_metrics(kcv_run(p, folds = fold_blocks(~ x + y, meuse, blocks = 3)))
kcv_metrics(kcv_run(p, buffer = 300))
```

## Performance

Ordinary kriging on simulated data, 4-core laptop with OpenBLAS (median
seconds; from the scripts in `inst/bench/`):

| n | LOO: fastkcv / [`krige.cv()`](https://r-spatial.github.io/gstat/reference/krige.cv.html) | 5-fold: fastkcv / [`krige.cv()`](https://r-spatial.github.io/gstat/reference/krige.cv.html) |
|---:|:---|:---|
| 1,000 | 0.06 / 67 (1,100x) | 0.07 / 0.8 (12x) |
| 2,000 | 0.25 / 368 (1,500x) | 0.29 / 5.7 (19x) |
| 5,000 | 2.1 / not run | 2.6 / 85 (32x) |

The gain is largest for leave-one-out and smallest for a few large
folds. [`kcv()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv.md)
handles n = 20,000 in about two minutes.

The vignette ([Get
started](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/articles/fastkcv.md))
covers the fold designs, buffered leave-one-out, precomputed covariance
matrices, and the performance and memory notes.

## Scope

Global kriging only: every observation is in the kriging neighborhood.
Local neighborhoods (`nmax`, `nmin`, `maxdist`), block kriging,
unbounded variograms, geographic coordinates and re-fitting the
variogram in each fold are not supported, and give an error. Memory is
one n x n matrix (8 n^2 bytes, 3.2 GB at n = 20,000), checked before
anything is allocated.

## Related packages

fastkcv is a companion to gstat, not a fork or a replacement:
[`kcv()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv.md) takes
the inputs of
[`krige.cv()`](https://r-spatial.github.io/gstat/reference/krige.cv.html)
and returns its output, and fitting variograms and kriging new locations
stay with gstat. It is a separate package for three reasons. The single
factorization works only for global kriging, while gstat’s engine sets
up a kriging system for each prediction location, which is what makes
local neighborhoods (`nmax`, `maxdist`) possible. It needs compiled C++
code (Rcpp, RcppArmadillo) and a dense n x n matrix (8 n^2 bytes,
checked up front). And most of the package is a cross-validation toolkit
rather than a faster
[`krige.cv()`](https://r-spatial.github.io/gstat/reference/krige.cv.html):
buffered leave-one-out, spatial fold builders,
[`kcv_metrics()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_metrics.md),
[`kcv_prepare()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_prepare.md)
/
[`kcv_run()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_prepare.md)
to reuse one factorization, and
[`kcv_engine()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_engine.md)
for any covariance matrix.

`leaveOneOut.km()` in DiceKriging uses the same closed-form
leave-one-out algebra, without a nugget term, with tensor-product
kernels on a design matrix rather than gstat variogram models on spatial
data, and without k-fold or buffered designs. From the same covariance
matrix, fastkcv is 1.6 to 4.1 times faster end to end (OpenBLAS) and
about level on the leave-one-out step alone. blockCV and spatialsample
build spatial folds for any model but do not fit one; a partition from
them, such as `folds_ids` from blockCV’s `cv_spatial()`, can be passed
to `kcv_run(folds = )`.

|  | LOO | k-fold | Buffered LOO | Block / cluster folds | Nugget, gstat models | Input | Exact, no refit per fold |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| fastkcv | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | data.frame, `sf`, `sp` | yes |
| gstat [`krige.cv()`](https://r-spatial.github.io/gstat/reference/krige.cv.html) | yes | yes | no | any fold vector | yes | data.frame, `sf`, `sp` | no (refits) |
| DiceKriging `leaveOneOut.km()` | yes | no | no | no | no | design matrix | yes |
| blockCV | NNDM variant | yes | yes | yes | (folds only) | `sf`, `sp` points | (folds only) |
| spatialsample | yes (`v = Inf`) | yes | yes | yes | (folds only) | `sf` | (folds only) |

## Use of AI tools

This package was developed with the help of an AI coding assistant
(Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5), used for writing and reviewing code,
tests and documentation. The author directed the work and is responsible
for the package; its results are checked against
[`gstat::krige.cv()`](https://r-spatial.github.io/gstat/reference/krige.cv.html)
and independent R implementations by the test suite.

# Package index

## Cross-validation

[`kcv()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv.md) is
[`gstat::krige.cv()`](https://r-spatial.github.io/gstat/reference/krige.cv.html)
from one factorization;
[`kcv_prepare()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_prepare.md)
and
[`kcv_run()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_prepare.md)
reuse that factorization for any number of fold designs and responses.

- [`kcv()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv.md) :
  Fast exact cross-validation for global kriging
- [`kcv_prepare()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_prepare.md)
  [`kcv_run()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_prepare.md)
  : Factorize once, cross-validate many times

## Fold designs

Random, spatial block and k-means folds for `nfold` or `folds`.

- [`fold_random()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/folds.md)
  [`fold_blocks()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/folds.md)
  [`fold_kmeans()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/folds.md)
  : Fold builders for cross-validation

## Summaries

- [`kcv_metrics()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_metrics.md)
  : Summary statistics of a cross-validation

## Precomputed covariance matrix

The same computation from any covariance matrix.

- [`kcv_engine()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_engine.md)
  [`kcv_engine_prepare()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_engine.md)
  [`kcv_engine_run()`](https://n-c-taylor.github.io/fastkcv/reference/kcv_engine.md)
  : Exact kriging cross-validation from a covariance matrix
